analysis.title: Iron Mountain Inc. (IRM): Mixed 3Q, but growth across data centers, ALM and digital solutions supports a healthy multi-year outlook
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on IRM with a 12-month price target of $136, cut from $155, against a $118.66 price (14.6% upside). The cut comes from a lower target multiple of 19.0x AFFO/shr (22.5x prior) on REIT peer multiple contraction as rates rise.
3Q26 results were mixed. AFFO/shr of $1.53 beat GS at $1.45 and consensus at $1.48, and 2026 guidance was raised. Revenue of $1,991mn (+13.5% y/y) was in line with FactSet consensus growth of 13.6%.

Record data center leasing of 102 MW in 3Q brings YTD leasing to 137 MW. IRM expects 2027 data center revenue above $1.3bn (20%+ growth), and the signed backlog supports nearly 40% further growth once fully developed, before any new leasing or pricing.

India was 74 MW (~73%) of 3Q data center leasing. Development yields are 200-300 bps above IRM's typical 10-12% unlevered return range at the low end, and potentially meaningfully higher, because lower construction costs more than offset lower leasing rates.

Asset lifecycle management (ALM) revenue grew 38% y/y organically in 3Q, with Enterprise ALM up more than 50%. IRM expects ALM revenue to modestly exceed $1bn in 2026 and 25%+ organic growth in 2027, assuming memory pricing stays flat.

Digital solutions: the US Treasury contract should add $100-150mn of revenue in 2027, up from $40-45mn in 2026. IRM handles ~95% of the IRS forms covered by the program and is one of two vendors. Insight DXP also won its largest deployment to date, a Middle Eastern government rollout across 30 agencies, and Standard Chartered began a first phase in Asia-Pacific.

RIM storage organic revenue grew 5% y/y, or more than 7% excluding a prior-year data management benefit, the strongest underlying growth in more than two years. Organic volumes were stable to up slightly, and pricing and revenue management drove growth.
AFFO/shr rose 16% y/y, supporting a 15% dividend increase with the trailing payout ratio below 60%. Net lease-adjusted leverage was 4.8x, the lowest since before IRM's REIT conversion.

Growth is moderating. Reported revenue growth slowed to 13.5% in 3Q from 18.5% in 2Q, partly because a ~$30mn data center decommissioning project shifted from 3Q into 2Q. The 4Q outlook implies ~10% reported revenue growth.
ALM growth in 2027 depends mostly on volume because elevated memory prices have been stable since 4Q 2025. Faster ALM growth would also dilute consolidated EBITDA margin because ALM is lower margin.

2026 guidance was raised: revenue to $7,950-8,020mn (from $7,940-8,010mn), EBITDA to $2,948-2,978mn (from $2,945-2,975mn, margin 37.1% unchanged) and AFFO/shr to $5.94-6.00 (from $5.87-5.93). GS says this points to lower consensus revenue estimates and higher consensus EBITDA and AFFO/shr estimates.

GS raises 2026/2027/2028 AFFO/shr estimates to $5.98/$6.71/$7.33 from $5.91/$6.55/$7.21. It cuts adjusted EPS for 2026/2027/2028 to $2.52/$2.77/$3.04 from $2.57/$2.93/$3.27, and revenue is essentially unchanged.

market_movers.rationale: Data center, ALM and digital solutions growth tied to AI demand, plus durable RIM storage cash generation, drives valuation upside. The price target falls from $155 on a lower REIT peer multiple.

earnings_insights: IRM 3Q26 (reported 11/5/2026): revenue $1,991mn, +13.5% y/y vs GS estimate of +13.0% and FactSet consensus of +13.6%. Organic growth was 12.8% vs GS estimate of 11.5% and 16.8% in the prior quarter.
IRM 3Q26 adjusted EPS $0.64 reported, in line with GS estimate $0.64 and above FactSet consensus $0.61. GAAP EPS was $0.41.

IRM 3Q26 AFFO/shr $1.53 reported vs GS estimate $1.45 and FactSet consensus $1.48, up 15.8% y/y. Adjusted EBITDA margin was 37.6%, flat y/y, in line with GS estimate and slightly above consensus of 37.5%.
IRM 3Q26 segment organic growth: data center +34.3% y/y, Corporate and Other (including ALM) +30.7%, RIM +6.7% with storage +5.2% and services +9.0%.

IRM 2026 guidance raised: AFFO/shr $5.94-6.00 (prior $5.87-5.93). Before the print GS forecast 2026 AFFO/shr of $5.91 and FactSet consensus was $5.92. GS forecast 2026 revenue of $7,995mn and consensus was $8,037mn.
IRM implied 4Q26 reported revenue growth is ~10%. GS 4Q26E revenue is $2,040mn (+10.7% y/y), adjusted EPS $0.69 and AFFO/shr $1.58.
GS FY2027E revenue $8,764mn (+9.6%), adjusted EBITDA $3,258mn, AFFO/shr $6.71. FY2028E revenue $9,499mn, adjusted EBITDA $3,539mn, AFFO/shr $7.33.

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS cut its IRM target multiple to 19.0x from 22.5x to reflect lower REIT peer multiples as rates rise.

risk_factors: India leasing concentration (~73% of 3Q data center leasing) raises execution risk, including land ownership diligence and aggregating adjacent parcels.
ALM growth in 2027 relies on volume, customer expansion, cross-selling and share gains with no further memory price increases, and it dilutes EBITDA margin.
Near-term growth is moderating, with 4Q implying ~10% reported revenue growth.
Stated downside risks: competing technologies in records management, acquisition integration, financial leverage and FX.
Transformation from a legacy records management company to a data and technology company carries execution risk and medium-term financial uncertainty.

tension_points.bull_case: Record 102 MW leasing supports 20%+ data center revenue growth in 2027 with signed backlog adding nearly 40% more. ALM is guided to 25%+ organic growth and the US Treasury contract ramps to $100-150mn.
tension_points.bear_case: 4Q implies ~10% reported revenue growth. India is ~73% of 3Q leasing, and ALM growth depends on volume with flat memory prices and dilutes margin.
tension_points.what_invalidates: ALM organic growth below the 25%+ 2027 outlook with memory pricing flat, or delays in India development from land diligence problems.
